Regulation: B.C. Reg. 131/2026
Made under: Miscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 17, 2026

B.C. Reg. 131/2026, deposited July 17, 2026, under theMISCELLANEOUS STATUTES AMENDMENT ACT, 2026[section 33] andUNIVERSITY ENDOWMENT LAND ACT[section 14 (2)]. Order in Council 338/2026, approved and ordered July 17, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that (a)	sections 17 to 21, 23 and 24 of theMiscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act, 2026, S.B.C. 2026, c. 15, are brought into force, and (b)	the attached University Endowment Land Bylaw Enforcement Ticket Regulation is made. — C. BOYLE,Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs; N. SHARMA,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. UNIVERSITY ENDOWMENT LAND BYLAWENFORCEMENT TICKET REGULATION "Act"means theUniversity Endowment Land Act; "UEL bylaw"means a bylaw enacted by the minister under section 12 (1) of the Act; "young person"has the same meaning as in section 1 of theYouth Justice Act. 2The following are the maximum amounts of fines that may be imposed under a UEL bylaw: (a)	$3 000, unless paragraph (b) applies; (b)	$1 000, if a young person is charged with an offence that is dealt with under Division 3 of Part 8 of theCommunity Charter. Prescribed classes of bylaw enforcement officers 3The following are the prescribed classes of persons who may be designated as bylaw enforcement officers for the purpose of the enforcement of a UEL bylaw: (a)	members, other than civilian members, of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police; (i)	who are employees, as defined in section 1 of thePublic Service Act, and (ii)	whose duties include the enforcement of one or more UEL bylaws; (i)	who are employees of a corporation retained by the government for the purpose of the enforcement of one or more UEL bylaws, and (ii)	whose duties as employees of the corporation include the enforcement of one or more UEL bylaws. Prescribed forms of tickets and their content

minutes_briefs.title: New UEL bylaw ticket rules set $3,000 maximum fine and allow RCMP and contracted officers to enforce
minutes_briefs.summary: A new regulation under BC's University Endowment Land Act sets the maximum fines that can be imposed under University Endowment Land (UEL) bylaws at $3,000, or $1,000 when a young person is charged under the Community Charter process. It also lists who can be appointed as bylaw enforcement officers: RCMP members (excluding civilian staff), provincial government employees whose duties include enforcing UEL bylaws, and employees of a company hired by the government to enforce them. The regulation also prescribes the forms of tickets and what they must contain.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you operate on University Endowment Land, check your local UEL bylaws and ticket forms to confirm you understand the new $3,000 maximum fine and who can enforce it.
